# Apple’s Most Important Filing in 2025: What Apple SEC Filings Reveal
By [Admin](https://www.secfilingdata.com/blog/author/abdur/) · Oct 21, 2026 · 5 min read
![Apple’s Most Important Filing in 2025: What Apple SEC Filings Reveal](data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB3aWR0aD0iMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIxIiB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciPjwvc3ZnPg==)
Among Apple SEC filings submitted during calendar 2025, the most useful single document for understanding the company’s full-year position is its annual report on Form 10-K.
Filed on October 31, 2025, the report covers Apple’s fiscal year ended September 27, 2025.
That distinction matters: the filing arrived in calendar 2025, but its reporting period did not run from January through December.
## Why this is the most important Apple SEC filing of 2025
“Most important” is an editorial judgment, not an SEC ranking.
I chose the 2025 10-K because it covers a complete fiscal year, compares results with prior years, and combines financial data with discussion of risks, liquidity, and legal matters.
That breadth makes it a useful single-file overview.
Apple also filed 10-Q reports during 2025, including for the quarters ended March 29 and June 28.
These interim reports offer timely snapshots, while the 10-K provides a full-year view and deeper annual notes and risk discussion.
The official [Apple 2025 Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/000032019325000079/aapl-20250927.htm) identifies the form and fiscal year on its cover.
Apple’s fiscal year follows a 52- or 53-week calendar ending on the last Saturday of September.
Fiscal 2025 had 52 weeks, so the September 27 reporting date is the end of Apple’s fiscal year—not the end of calendar 2025.
## What the 10-K contains and how to navigate it
This helps prevent any single metric from standing in for the whole story.
Net income, for example, should be read alongside taxes, cash flow, and operating costs.
## Revenue: services grew faster, while product lines diverged
Apple reported fiscal 2025 net sales of $416.2 billion, up about 6% from $391.0 billion in fiscal 2024.
The filing separates sales into product categories and Services, which makes it possible to see which parts contributed to the change.
Amounts below are in U.S. dollars, rounded to the nearest billion; the 10-K reports exact amounts in millions.
| Category | Fiscal 2025 sales | Change from fiscal 2024 |
| iPhone | $209.6 billion | +4% |
| Mac | $33.7 billion | +12% |
| iPad | $28.0 billion | +5% |
| Wearables, Home and Accessories | $35.7 billion | −4% |
| Services | $109.2 billion | +14% |
| **Total net sales** | **$416.2 billion** | **+6%** |
Services include advertising, the App Store, and cloud services.
Apple attributed its increase primarily to higher sales from those areas.
It also includes recognized revenue from some services bundled with product sales, so it is not limited to standalone subscriptions or downloads.
## Profit and cash flow tell different parts of the story
Apple reported net income of $112.0 billion for fiscal 2025, compared with $93.7 billion in fiscal 2024.
Its effective income tax rate was 15.6%, down from 24.1%.
That context matters: the increase in net income should not be read as a simple measure of operating growth alone.
Apple generated $111.5 billion in cash from operating activities during fiscal 2025, compared with $118.3 billion in 2024.
Operating cash flow adjusts net income for noncash items and changes in operating assets and liabilities, so it can move differently from profit.
The statement also shows payments for share repurchases and dividends, alongside investment in property and equipment.
As of September 27, 2025, Apple reported $132.4 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities.
This is a year-end balance, not cash generated during the year.
## Geographic results and business exposure
Apple reports five geographic segments: Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan, and Rest of Asia Pacific.
Segment reporting shows where sales are attributed and how management organizes and reviews the business.
The Americas was the largest segment in fiscal 2025, at $178.4 billion in net sales; Europe reported $111.0 billion, and Greater China $64.4 billion.
Greater China sales declined, Apple said, primarily because of lower iPhone sales, partly offset by higher Mac sales.
The Americas, Europe, Japan, and Rest of Asia Pacific increased, with iPhone and Services contributing to several regions’ growth.
Segment revenue shows geographic exposure, though this table does not show each region’s profitability.
Apple described U.S. antitrust litigation, including the Department of Justice case and related lawsuits, as well as the Epic Games matter.

The report states that on April 30, 2025, a California federal court found Apple in violation of an injunction in the Epic case and imposed restrictions concerning fees and how developers direct users to outside payment options; Apple said it appealed.
The filing also discusses investigations relating to App Store terms in Europe and other jurisdictions.
For a focused walkthrough, see [how to search for a specific 10-K filing](https://www.secfilingdata.com/blog/how-to-search-for-a-specific-10-k-filing/).

**Takeaway: Apple’s fiscal 2025 Form 10-K is the strongest single starting point among its 2025 filings because it links a complete year of results with the risks, cash commitments, and legal disclosures that help explain them.** It is a detailed record of the year, not a promise about the next one. Readers can use it to frame better questions, then revisit newer filings as the company reports additional periods and material events.

**Apple's headquarters is Apple Park, at One Apple Park Way, Cupertino, California 95014 — a 175-acre campus that has served as the company's operational and executive center since April 2017.** Beyond Cupertino, Apple maintains major offices across the United States and in more than 25 countries, making it one of the most geographically distributed technology companies in the world.
**Key takeaways**
* International offices span EMEA, APAC, and Latin America, with regional hubs in London, Singapore, and Shanghai.
* Apple's office footprint is a useful prospecting signal for B2B sales teams targeting enterprise technology buyers.
## Where is Apple headquartered?
Apple is headquartered in Cupertino, California, in the heart of Silicon Valley.
The current campus, Apple Park, replaced the original Infinite Loop headquarters that Apple occupied from 1993.
* **General web:** [apple.com](https://www.apple.com)
## What Apple offices are in California?
California is home to Apple's densest office concentration.
Outside of Apple Park and the legacy Infinite Loop campus in Cupertino, Apple has significant presences across the Bay Area and in Southern California.
### Cupertino — Apple Park & Infinite Loop
The two Cupertino campuses collectively house the majority of Apple's hardware engineering, software engineering, operations, finance, legal, and executive teams.

Apple Park alone spans 175 acres and was reported to have cost approximately $5 billion to construct, according to [reporting by The New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2017/05/17/technology/apple-park-headquarters-opens.html).
### Sunnyvale
### San Diego

Apple's San Diego office focuses on wireless modem and chip design — a function that became strategically critical after Apple's acquisition of the majority of Intel's smartphone modem business in 2019 for approximately $1 billion.
### Los Angeles & Culver City
Apple TV+ content operations, along with its advertising technology and media teams, are based in the Los Angeles area.
The Culver City office in particular has grown significantly since Apple's push into original content for Apple TV+.
## Does Apple have offices outside California?
Yes — and at significant scale.
Apple's Austin campus is its largest U.S. presence outside California.

In 2018, Apple announced a $1 billion investment to expand the Austin facility, which now spans approximately 3 million square feet and employs more than 6,000 people in roles including engineering, sales operations, finance, and customer support.
Apple has been in Austin since 1992, making it one of the company's longest-running U.S. office locations outside the Bay Area.
### New York City, New York
Apple's New York offices span multiple locations in Manhattan, primarily housing advertising sales, media, financial services partnerships, and enterprise sales teams.
Apple's flagship Fifth Avenue retail store, which opened in 2006, is separate from its corporate offices but is among the most visited Apple locations globally.
Apple operates in over 25 countries with international offices ranging from regional headquarters to engineering centers and sales operations.

According to [Statista's workforce data](https://www.statista.com/statistics/273439/number-of-full-time-apple-employees-since-2005/), Apple employed approximately 150,000 full-time employees globally as of its most recent fiscal year — a headcount distributed across a substantial international footprint.
### Europe, Middle East & Africa (EMEA)
### Asia-Pacific (APAC)
* **Singapore:** Apple's APAC regional headquarters. Singapore houses operations, finance, and enterprise sales leadership for the Asia-Pacific region.

* **Shanghai, China:** Apple's Greater China commercial headquarters. China remains one of Apple's largest revenue markets, and the Shanghai office coordinates retail, supply chain, and commercial operations across the region.
* **Beijing, China:** Engineering and R&D operations, including a machine learning research center.
* **Tokyo, Japan:** Commercial and engineering operations. Japan is a key market for Apple hardware and services.
* **Sydney, Australia:** Commercial, operations, and AppleCare support for Australia and New Zealand.
* **São Paulo, Brazil:** Brazil commercial headquarters, supporting Apple's retail and commercial operations in South America's largest market.
## Why do sales teams research Apple office locations?
Understanding where Apple operates is more than a lookup exercise — it's a prospecting signal.
If you're selling to companies that work with Apple or that use Apple-adjacent technology stacks, knowing where Apple concentrates headcount tells you where supplier demand clusters.
This kind of location-based competitor and account research is exactly what tools like [Stealery](https://getstealery.com) are built to accelerate.

If you want to identify companies using a specific technology vendor — filtered by geography, company size, or hiring signals — you can pull that list in seconds rather than spending hours stitching together LinkedIn searches and job board data.
For reps building territory plans around specific metro areas or enterprise accounts, it's a meaningful shortcut.
